speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
text: asked the Minister for Manpower regarding the recent acquisition of Singapore-based AI start-up Manus (a) what percentage of the company's core workforce comprised Singapore citizens prior to the acquisition; (b) whether the acquisition terms include guarantees for local headcount retention or technology transfer; and (c) how the Ministry ensures that foreign-founded start-ups benefitting from Singapore's business environment facilitate skills transfer to local workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: These companies can also tap on reskilling and upskilling support from Workforce Singapore and SkillsFuture Singapore to equip our Singaporeans with the capabilities needed to take on new growth job roles.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have three supplementary questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Just to set the context, Manus AI is an example of a company that was redomiciled to Singapore from another jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The timeline was they were launched in March of last year, moved to Singapore in around the middle of the year and the acquisition was announced in December.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, one cannot help but feel that Singapore's business environment was taken advantage of opportunistically to achieve certain aims and then now, being cast aside.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, my three supplementary questions are: regarding redomiciled companies, are they subject to any targets on hiring Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second follow-up supplementary question: if they are, what timelines are they expected to comply with in order to meet these targets, after redomiciling?

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And finally, does MOM have any considerations to discourage companies from using Singapore as a flag of convenience, without accruing any benefits to the Singapore labour force?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I am mindful that time is running out, so, I will keep my reply short.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: All companies operating in Singapore ought to comply with Singapore labour laws.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Senior Minister of State Koh, I believe you wanted to make a clarification.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
